newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal says strong U.S. economy aided Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Portugal says strong U.S. economy aided Clinton.

text.p: Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres congratulated President Bill Clinton on his re-election, attributing the victory to a strong U.S. economic performance over the past four years.

Guterres, speaking on Tuesday night during an official four-day visit to Mexico, said he hoped the Clinton administration would be able to overcome its political differences with the still Republican-dominated U.S. Congress.
"The fact that the U.S. economy is clearly better today than four years ago was a vital component in the re-election," Guterres told TSF radio.

Guterres told the Portuguese news agency Lusa that he hoped Clinton's re-election would lead to increased pressure on the Indonesian government to "agree to abandon positions of rigidity" on the thorny issue of East Timor. Portugal is pressing for self-determination for the former Portuguese colony of East Timor, annexed by Indonesia in 1976.
